description_preview:
Introduction
Welcome to Gallagher - a global community of people who bring bold ideas, deep expertise, and a shared commitment to doing what’s right. We help clients navigate complexity with confidence by empowering businesses, communities, and individuals to thrive. At Gallagher, you’ll find more than a job; you’ll find a culture built on trust, driven by collaboration, and sustained by the belief that we’re better together. Whether you join us in a client-facing role or as part of our brokerage division, our benefits and HR consulting division, or our corporate team, you’ll have the opportunity to grow your career, make an impact, and be part of something bigger. Experience a workplace where you’re encouraged to be yourself, supported to succeed, and inspired to keep learning. That’s what it means to live The Gallagher Way.
Overview
The
AI
Developer
builds and ships the components that make Gallagher's enterprise AI solutions work. You will write production C#/.NET and Python code for RAG pipelines, AI agents, and Copilot integrations on our Azure stack, working from designs set by senior engineers while taking full ownership of the features assigned to you. This is a hands-on individual contributor role built for someone who learns fast, asks good questions, and turns what they learn into working software - in a regulated insurance environment where correctness, security, and auditability matter as much as speed.
How You'll Make An Impact
Build Production AI Features: Implement well-scoped components of GenAI and agentic systems - retrieval pipelines, tool integrations, prompt flows, API endpoints - in C#/.NET and Python, following the team's established patterns.
Integrate Across the Azure Stack: Wire AI capabilities into enterprise services using Azure AI Foundry, Azure OpenAI, Azure AI Search, Azure Functions, and Container Apps; connect to line-of-business systems through secure REST APIs and AI agents.
Ship to Enterprise Surfaces: Deliver working features into internal applications and support them once they are live.
Test and Evaluate Your Own Work: Write unit and integration tests, run the team's evaluation harnesses against your changes, and validate groundedness, accuracy, latency, and cost before asking for reviews.
Participate in Code and Design Reviews: Submit clean, reviewable pull requests, act on feedback quickly, and read others' code to learn the codebase and the standards behind it.
Follow Governance by Default: Apply the team's responsible-AI controls - Entra ID/RBAC, data-residency requirements, audit logging, human-in-the-loop checkpoints - as part of building the feature.
Debug and Support What You Build: Investigate production issues in AI pipelines and integrations, use logs and telemetry to isolate root causes, and deliver fixes with the same rigor as new features.
Learn Continuously and Apply It: Track how the AI tooling landscape is moving, run small experiments against real Gallagher problems, and bring what works back to the team with a clear explanation of why.
Communicate Clearly: Give honest status in stand-ups, flag blockers early, document what you built, and explain your work in terms teammates and business partners can follow.
About You
Experience: 1-3 years of professional software engineering experience (internships and co-ops count), or a strong equivalent portfolio of shipped work.
Languages: Working proficiency in C#/.NET, Python, Typescript and Javascript, with the ability to become strong in .NET and Python; comfortable reading unfamiliar code.
Cloud Fundamentals: Hands-on experience building or deploying on Azure (Functions, App Service, Container Apps, or equivalent), including authentication and configuration basics.
AI Exposure: Practical experience calling LLM APIs and building something real with them - a RAG prototype, an agent, a chatbot, or an internal tool - whether at work, at school, or on your own.
API and Data Skills: Building and consuming REST APIs, working with JSON, and querying relational or vector data stores.
Engineering Hygiene: Git-based workflow, familiarity with CI/CD pipelines (Azure DevOps or equivalent), and a habit of testing your own work.
Education: Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field - or demonstrable equivalent experience.
Preferred Differentiators
Microsoft AI Ecosystem: Exposure to Azure infrastructure, Microsoft Foundry, Copilot Studio, Microsoft Agent Framework, or LangChain.
Regulated Industry Awareness: Any experience - internship, coursework, or prior role - in insurance, financial services, or healthcare, where compliance shapes how software is built.
AI-Assisted Development: Fluent use of AI coding assistants and agent workflows to move faster without sacrificing code quality.
Evaluation Mindset: Experience writing evals, test sets, or benchmarks for LLM outputs rather than judging quality by eye.
Infrastructure Familiarity: Reading or contributing to Terraform and similar infrastructure-as-code.
Certifications: Azure certifications such as AZ-204, AI-102, or AI-900 are beneficial.
Professional Qualities
Relentlessly Curious: Digs into how things actually work rather than stopping at the first answer; treats unfamiliar territory as the interesting part of the job.
Learns and applies: Converts new knowledge into shipped work quickly - the reading, the course, and the side experiment show up in the codebase and not just in conversation.
Ownership Over Assignment: Takes a task through to working software in users' hands, including the unglamorous parts: tests, edge cases, documentation, and cleanup.
Ask Early, Unblock Fast: Attempts a solution independently, then raises a specific, well-framed question before burning a day on the wrong path.
Receptive to Feedback: Treats code review as the fastest way to get better; separates critique of the code from critique of the person.
Careful in a Regulated Setting: Understands that Gallagher's AI touches client and bus

description_preview:
Since we opened our doors in 2009, the world of commerce has evolved immensely, and so has Square. After enabling anyone to take payments and never miss a sale, we saw sellers stymied by disparate, outmoded products and tools that wouldn’t work together.
So we expanded into software and started building integrated, omnichannel solutions – to help sellers sell online, manage inventory, offer buy now, pay later functionality, book appointments, engage loyal buyers, and hire and pay staff. Across it all, we’ve embedded financial services tools at the point of sale, so merchants can access a business loan and manage their cash flow in one place. Afterpay furthers our goal to provide omnichannel tools that unlock meaningful value and growth, enabling sellers to capture the next generation shopper, increase order sizes, and compete at a larger scale.
Today, we are a partner to sellers of all sizes – large, enterprise-scale businesses with complex operations, sellers just starting, as well as merchants who began selling with Square and have grown larger over time. As our sellers grow, so do our solutions. There is a massive opportunity in front of us. We’re building a significant, meaningful, and lasting business, and we are helping sellers worldwide do the same.
The Role
You will join the Recon and Reporting team, which owns our post-transaction systems: the platform responsible for reconciling money, tracing the end-to-end flow of funds, and meeting our tax and regulatory reporting obligations to merchants, customers, and authorities worldwide. Reconciliation and financial reporting are essential to running a payments business, and given our transaction volume, the projects you own will have direct, measurable impact on financial accuracy and trust.
You will help build and operate the systems that ingest and integrate global card-network settlement and report files (Visa, Mastercard, and equivalents), along with data from acquirers, processors, and banks, and reconcile them against internal payment data to power settlement, dispute, cost, tax, and regulatory reporting. You will own well-scoped projects within this platform end-to-end, with guidance from more experienced engineers. Our vision is to make reconciliation and reporting accurate, automated, and near real-time.
You Will
Own small, well-bounded projects end-to-end with guidance available: clarify requirements, design, build, test, ship, and follow up.
Build and maintain features within the ingestion and reconciliation pipelines that match card-network and partner reports against internal transaction data.

Develop features for reporting and reconciliation products that are accurate, reliable, timely, scalable, and user-friendly for both internal finance teams and external merchants.
Produce standardized journals and summaries that feed downstream accounting, audit, and analysis.
Contribute to our large-scale tax and regulatory reporting systems, including US IRS information returns (the 1099 family, issued at the scale of tens of millions of forms annually to merchants and customers) and international regimes such as EU-wide CESOP and country-specific reporting for Australia, Ireland, and Spain.
Support broader regulatory and compliance obligations (AML, KYC, and similar), with careful handling of sensitive and PII data, including TIN validation and secure form generation and filing.
Validate your work before calling it done, using code review, tests, small experiments, or usage signals, including for AI-assisted changes.
Take agency in debugging and escalating production issues across services, giving the team clear context on what changed, when it changed, how it changed, and what risk remains.

description_preview:
The Role
We're hiring Software Engineers to join FLINT's Intelligence team. This is an early-career position, designed for someone with 0–2 years of professional experience (recent graduates and strong interns welcome) who wants to grow fast by building things that matter.
Software Engineers at FLINT work alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers (FDEs). FDEs sit with the business, elicit requirements, and own the design and architecture of what we build. Software Engineers take that design and turn it into working, tested, documented software on Foundry — and push back when the design doesn't hold up. You'll have a clear owner to learn from and a steady stream of well-scoped work to ship.
This is a foundational role with mentorship built in and a defined path forward — first through the Software Engineer levels, and then, for those who develop real fluency in how FLINT operates, into the Forward Deployed Engineer track.
AI-Native by Default
We believe the teams moving fastest right now are the ones where AI is doing the bulk of the code writing, testing, and drafting, with engineers directing and verifying the work rather than typing it out. We're building FLINT's Intelligence team that way, and we screen for it.
What AI-native looks like here:
You start from a spec, not a blank editor. You use AI tools to draft, generate, and refactor code, then read it critically.
You use AI to test at scale — generating scenarios, edge cases, and validation you'd never have time to write by hand.
You treat your AI session as a production surface and Foundry as the system of record: work happens in the session, results land in the system.
You can explain what the AI did, why it's right, and where it's wrong. Speed without judgment doesn't count.
If this is already how you work, you'll feel at home. If you're curious but haven't built this way yet, tell us — we'd rather teach a curious engineer than hire a fast one who won't learn.
What You'll Do
Build applications, workflows, and pipelines on Palantir Foundry that make FLINT's data accessible, reliable, and actionable for project and manufacturing teams.
Write and maintain Python to transform, clean, normalize, and connect data from the systems we run the company on — Autodesk Construction Cloud, Revit, Revizto, Oracle Primavera Cloud, and Sage Intacct, among others.
Work with APIs and common data formats (JSON, CSV, XML) to integrate systems and automate processes end to end.
Take well-defined work from FDEs and deliver it to a clear definition of done — then ask the questions that make the next definition better.
Contribute to FLINT's ontology: the objects, relationships, and standards that let knowledge compound across projects.
Document code, workflows, and applications so the team (and the company) can build on what you built.
Support release cycles to beta testers in the field, and fold their feedback back into the build.
What We're Looking For
0–2 years of professional experience coding in Python (internships and substantial personal projects count).
Demonstrated AI-native working habits: you can show us how you use AI tools to design, build, and test software, and how you verify the output.

Strong engineers from top tech companies are actively encouraged to apply. No finance background required. If you've done serious systems work at a place with a high bar, that's exactly the profile.

Engineers work alongside traders and researchers to design and ship the infrastructure behind automated trading strategies: pricing engines, execution systems, real-time risk, and the data pipelines feeding all of it. Are you interested in developing software or advancing radar and radio-frequency systems for critical national security challenges?
Do you enjoy understanding how complex systems work, testing ideas against evidence, and turning technical concepts into useful capabilities?
If so, we’re looking for someone like you to join our team at APL!
We are a multidisciplinary team of engineers, scientists, mathematicians, and software developers who advance electromagnetic and computer-system capabilities for critical national security missions, with a primary focus on maritime applications. Our work spans radar, electronic warfare (EW), RF communications and propagation, remote sensing, signal and image processing, software development, modeling and simulation, and technical prototyping.
We bring domain experts, analysts, algorithm developers, and software engineers together to carry ideas from initial analysis and concept development through implementation, integration, test, and evaluation. We are seeking engineers, computer scientists, mathematicians, and physicists with strong technical fundamentals who want to contribute in one or both of the areas described below.
We value people who ask thoughtful questions, take initiative when the path forward is not obvious, test assumptions against evidence, seek out expertise when needed, and follow through to technically sound, useful results. The breadth of our work provides opportunities to build deep expertise, contribute across adjacent disciplines, and grow into technical or project leadership.
As a member of our team, you will...
Work with multidisciplinary teams to understand operational needs, formulate technical problems, and develop practical approaches.
Develop software, models, algorithms, analysis tools, experiments, or prototypes appropriate to the problem.
Use simulated, laboratory, and real-world data to understand system behavior, evaluate performance, and guide further development.
Contribute across multiple stages of the development lifecycle and clearly communicate your work through code, documentation, technical discussions, presentations, and reports.

Software Development
Design, implement, test, document, and maintain software applications, analysis tools, and technical prototypes.
Develop software that processes sensor data, supports modeling and simulation, or interfaces with hardware, networks, and distributed systems.
Apply an understanding of computer architecture, operating systems, networks, protocols, and software behavior to understand how complex systems communicate, perform, and fail and to improve their security and resilience.
Work closely with algorithm developers and domain experts to mature technical concepts and research prototypes into reliable, maintainable, and efficient software.
RF Systems Engineering
Analyze and model radar, communications, EW, remote-sensing, propagation, and other RF systems.
Develop and evaluate signal-processing algorithms for detection, estimation, tracking, classification, and other sensor-data exploitation problems.
Use modeling, simulation, laboratory experiments, and field data to characterize system performance, understand limitations, and evaluate new concepts.
Develop technical prototypes and support algorithm, software, and hardware integration, test, and evaluation.
Qualifications
You meet our minimum qualifications for the job if you...
Have a Bachelor's or Master's degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, software engineering, mathematics, physics, or another closely related technical field.
Have programming experience through coursework, research, employment, or independent projects using languages such as C++, Python, Java, MATLAB, or similar.
Have a technical foundation in at least one of the following:
software development, computer systems, operating systems, or networking; or
electromagnetics, RF systems, communications, signal processing, or the mathematical or physical foundations underlying these areas.
Have demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills and the ability to apply technical fundamentals to unfamiliar problems.
Can work independently, collaborate effectively as part of a multidisciplinary team, and communicate technical ideas clearly.
Are willing and able to work in closed-area facilities.
Are able to obtain an Interim Secret security clearance by your start date and ultimately obtain a Top Secret/SCI security clearance. If selected, you will be subject to a government security-clearance investigation and must meet the requirements for access to classified information. Eligibility requirements include U.S. citizenship.
You’ll go above and beyond our minimum requirements if you...
Have completed an internship, capstone, thesis, research effort, independent project, or other substantial technical activity related to one or more of the areas described above.
Have experience with software-development or system-level computing practices such as object-oriented or systems programming, Linux, version control, automated testing, debugging, continuous integration, performance optimization, computer networking, embedded systems, or distributed systems.
Have coursework or project experience involving electromagnetics, radar, RF systems, communications, EW, propagation, antennas, remote sensing, or signal processing.
Have experience with modeling and simulation, scientific computing, numerical methods, data analysis, machine learning, or algorithm development.
Have experience integrating software with sensors, hardware, networks, laboratory equipment, or other real-world systems, or evaluating technical approaches through experiments, field tests, or benchmarking.
Have demonstrated initiative, follow-through, or emerging leadership by defining next steps, coordinating with others, seeking out need

About Graphon
Graphon AI is building the pre-model intelligence layer for the next generation of AI.
We are developing the context engine layer that solves a fundamental challenge:
“What if I could just dump all my data and GPT/Claude/Gemini could smartly reason across it?”
Today, this is incredibly difficult due to the limitations of LLM context windows and the fundamental squared scaling inherent to attention mechanisms. While sparse attention and RAG systems attempt to address this, they haven't proven to be robust general solutions.
Our Approach
Pre-model intelligence is our answer. We believe a graph-based approach that analyzes relationships across data on a topological level provides the correct inductive bias for long-context multimodal reasoning.
Just as
CNNs
provided the bias for spatial invariance in vision, and
Transformers
established the standard for sequential dependencies in language, our framework provides the structural foundation needed for complex, interconnected data.
We believe the next wave of AI progress will come from better infrastructure around models:
Better Memory & Context:
Creating truly persistent, scalable state.

Moving beyond simple embeddings to relational world models.
Universal Infrastructure:
A way to stop rebuilding the same context layer for every agent, dataset, and application.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.
EMBEDDED SECURITY ENGINEER (STARLINK)
At SpaceX we’re leveraging our experience in building rockets and spacecraft to deploy Starlink, the world’s most advanced broadband internet system. Starlink is the world’s largest satellite constellation and serves millions of users worldwide. We design, build, and operate all parts of the system – thousands of satellites and all of the space-ground infrastructure necessary for a constellation of that size. As we scale the constellation to hundreds of thousands of satellites, and become a foundation of global connectivity both on earth (and in space), we are looking for excellent engineers to help us build secure, defensible systems from the ground up.
Skills
In this role, you will influence the security of software across our space and terrestrial systems. Ideally, you have notable skills in one or more of the following:
Applied cryptography
Network security
Operating system security
Secure/Authenticated boot
Incident response and adversary detection
Vulnerability research
Software engineering
Responsibilities
Design and build security infrastructure for Starlink, including cryptographic services and other security-critical services
Develop security features for Starlink systems, including our router, dish, gateways, and satellites
Design security into factory processes and provide network services in support of this
Maintain existing production systems and improve security posture via both direct implementation and recommendations to other teams
Build prototypes and help identify, design, and test security improvements
Further our mission of providing secure and reliable Internet to underserved communities
Basic Qualifications
Bachelor's degree in computer science or another STEM discipline; OR 2+ years of professional experience in security software development in lieu of a degree
Experience with one or more software development languages (i.e. Python, C++, Golang)
Experience designing and implementing security solutions for operating systems, distributed systems, or other enterprise/large-scale infrastructure
Preferred Skills And Experience
Experience contributing security improvements to complex systems
Experience working with special purpose security hardware such as Trusted Platform Modules (TPMs) and Hardware Security Modules (HSMs)
Fundamental understanding of network protocols; including the TCP/IP stack as well as UDP based protocols
Experienced in navigating large, complex, interactive systems
Flexibility, communicating clearly, and establishing and maintaining productive working relationships with other engineering teams
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal
Ability to work both independently and in a team
Demonstrated ability to deal with ambiguity and to learn new technologies quickly
Advanced degree in a technical or engineering discipline

Must be willing to work extended hours and weekends as needed

This role will own and develop the services, APIs, and data infrastructure that connect ForgeNest’s Universal Operating System to machines, sensors, and the applications operators, engineers, and customers use to interact with them.
You’ll work directly with software engineers, robotics and controls engineers, manufacturing teams, and company leadership to design backend architecture, build reliable services and APIs, and contribute to the front-end applications those systems power.
Responsibilities
Design, build, and maintain backend services and APIs supporting ForgeNest’s manufacturing platform.
Architect and maintain data models, databases, and pipelines for machine data, production data, and operational data.
Integrate backend systems with ForgeNest’s Universal Operating System, machine controllers, sensors, and third-party tools.
Build reliable, secure, and scalable APIs consumed by front-end applications and other internal systems.
Develop the backend logic and data services behind dashboards and visualization tools that provide real-time insight into equipment status, production performance, and manufacturing workflows.
Partner directly with manufacturing, robotics, controls, and engineering teams to understand data and system requirements on the floor.
Participate in product architecture and technical design decisions as the platform continues to evolve.
Establish backend architecture, service design patterns, and development standards that support long-term scalability.
Monitor, troubleshoot, and improve system performance and reliability in both development and live manufacturing environments.
Rapidly prototype new backend functionality based on feedback from customers, operators, and internal engineering teams.
Contribute to front-end applications and components as needed, using JavaScript/TypeScript and React or similar frameworks, to help ship complete features.
Take ownership of features end-to-end, from backend design and data architecture through any necessary front-end integration.
Who You Are
A backend-minded software engineer who also enjoys working across the stack when a feature calls for it.
Excited about designing clean, reliable services and data systems while understanding the machines and manufacturing processes that data represents.
Comfortable owning a system end-to-end, from data model to API, with enough front-end fluency to see a feature through to the interface.
Able to communicate and collaborate across software, manufacturing, robotics, controls, and company leadership.
Motivated by building resilient infrastructure and seeing it power real-world systems.
Experience Requirements
Professional experience developing backend services, APIs, or distributed systems.
Strong proficiency with a backend language such as Node.js, Python, Go, or Java.
Experience designing and maintaining databases (SQL and/or NoSQL) and data models.
Experience building and integrating RESTful or event-driven APIs.
Working proficiency with front-end technologies, JavaScript and/or TypeScript and a framework such as React, sufficient to build or modify UI components.
Strong understanding of application architecture, service design, and state and data management across a stack.
Experience with real-time or data-rich systems such as dashboards, telemetry, or operational applications.
Strong debugging and problem-solving skills across the stack.
Experience working collaboratively within a software development team.
What You Bring
Strong ownership mentality and willingness to take features from concept through production.
Ability to operate effectively in a fast-moving startup environment.
Curiosity about manufacturing, robotics, industrial automation, and physical systems.
Strong systems-design instincts and attention to reliability, scalability, and data integrity.
Ability to simplify technically complex information without sacrificing functionality.
Comfortable picking up front-end work when needed, even when it isn’t your primary strength.
Experience with manufacturing software, industrial automation, robotics, machine interfaces, or real-time systems is a plus.
Experience with message queues, streaming data, or time-series databases is a plus.
Interest in AI-enabled software and how intelligent systems can improve physical manufacturing is highly valued.
What Success Looks Like
Quickly develop an understanding of ForgeNest’s technology and backend architecture, and how engineers and operators interact with the platform.
Take ownership of major backend systems and services, improving the reliability, scalability, and performance of the software experience.
Help establish backend architecture and development standards capable of scaling alongside ForgeNest’s technology and customer base.
Build APIs and services that make it straightforward for front-end teams, or yourself, to build reliable interfaces on top.
Become a trusted technical contributor as the software platform and engineering organization continue to grow.
Why Join ForgeNest
ForgeNest is a venture-backed startup building an AI-driven, software-forward forging platform designed to modernize one of the world’s most critical manufacturing industries.
By combining commercially available hardware with proprietary software, AI-driven toolpath generation, and a next-generation Universal Operating System, ForgeNest is transforming how forged metal parts are designed and manufactured across defense, aerospace, energy, maritime, and industrial markets.
